readme: DIFFERENTIAL vector suite for terrDVM's nostr geospatial protocol.
Every rule in CONTRACT.md that either language could get wrong is pinned
here as an explicit input/output pair. Both the TypeScript builders in
packages/geo-protocol/src and the Python builders in
services/blossom-gis/src/blossom_gis/geo_protocol.py MUST reproduce every
vector exactly. `content` is compared as a STRING, byte for byte, because
it is hashed into the event id.
This file replaces geo-protocol.json, which pinned ONE sample. A single
sample fixes one point in the input space and nothing else: it cannot see
validation, parsing, filter or number-formatting divergence, and all
eleven drift findings of the last review lived outside it. Worse, the test
that consumed it read the expected bbox out of the fixture and fed it back
into the builder, asserting the fixture equalled itself.
CONVENTIONS
- `expect` is the exact expected output. `reject` is an error CODE from
the table in CONTRACT.md; the message is free, the code is not.
- `{"__number__": "<token>"}` anywhere in a vector denotes a numeric
literal JSON cannot carry. Tokens: NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, -0.
Substitute the real value before feeding it to the implementation.
- Vectors under `validation.cases` are `validation.baseInput` with the
named keys replaced by `patch`. A patch value of null means the key is
ABSENT, not null-valued.
- `{"__json__": "NULL"}` is an EXPLICIT null, as distinct from the
absent-key spelling above. CONTRACT.md 7.5 rules the two equivalent
for `properties` and `description`; the tokens exist so a vector can
say which spelling it fed in.
- `grammar` pins the GRAMMAR rather than the values: the character
classes, the whitespace set and the validation ORDER. Every rule that
two languages spell with two different regexes lives there.
- Filter objects are compared structurally; key order is not significant
on the wire, but the order shown is the one CONTRACT.md mandates.
- Cover cell lists are ORDERED: longitude outer (west to east), latitude
inner (south to north). The order is part of the contract because the
filter it produces is compared as a whole.

socialGeohashLadder.note: NOT governed by the single-precision rule above. Kinds 1, 1063, 30315 and 31923 carry a LADDER of g tags — every prefix of the precision-6 geohash, shortest first. Nostr tag filters are exact string matches, so a client querying precision 5 (presence.ts:175) or precision 2/3/4 by viewport span (presence.ts:205-214) can never match a lone precision-4 tag. Collapsing these to one p4 tag is what silently killed live presence and the geo-note feed.
coverageArithmetic: A p4 cell is 20 bits: 10 lon + 10 lat = 0.3515625 x 0.17578125 deg
= 39.1 x 19.4 km at the equator, 27.7 x 19.5 km at 45N.
Continental Europe (-25,34,45,72) needs 201 x 217 = 43617 p4 cells.
The whole world needs 992200. cellsFor() caps at 48 — 0.1% coverage,
with no error anywhere. That is why the ladder exists.

shortest round-trip, not the exact binary value
JS and Python both print positionally here

readme: GRAMMAR vectors. The suite above pins VALUES; this section pins the
GRAMMAR that produces them — every place where the two languages spell
one rule with two different character classes.
Each case is `validation.baseInput` (builder: "item") or
`grammar.collectionBaseInput` (builder: "collection") with the named keys
replaced by `patch`, exactly like `validation.cases`. A patch value of
null means the key is ABSENT; `{"__json__": "NULL"}` means an explicit
null, which CONTRACT.md 7.5 rules is the same thing.
Lone surrogates travel as `{"__string__": "<TOKEN>"}`, never as a raw
\udXXX escape: the escape is legal JSON that both parsers accept, but the
TypeScript suite imports this file through a bundler that refuses it, and
a vector one side cannot even load pins nothing.
The `order-*` cases each carry TWO defects. They pin WHICH error code
wins, because CONTRACT.md 14 makes the code normative and 14.1 makes the
checking order normative with it.

exactTile.note: limit is 500, NOT 1: (kind, pubkey, d) lets several publishers hold the same d, and limit 1 would hide all but one

encode.note: the same point at full precision
null island; every division is hit exactly, and >= resolves upward
the south-west corner of the world
the north-east corner; both maxima take the >= branch
exactly on a p4 division from below

cover.name: single-cell
cover.note: 0.03 x 0.01 deg — smaller than one p4 cell, but it still straddles a boundary

cover.name: wider-than-one-cell
cover.note: 1.5 x 0.7 deg: 5 columns x 5 rows. Corner sampling returned at most 4 of these 25 and reported success.

cover.name: point
cover.note: degenerate viewport, west == east and south == north

cover.name: polar-above-mercator
cover.note: reaches past the Web Mercator cut-off of 85.05112878. Covering clamps to the GEOHASH domain (+/-90), not to the Mercator one — presence and geo-notes exist above 85 even though tiles do not. The extra rows simply come back empty.

cover.name: south-west-corner
cover.note: the origin cell of the grid

cover.name: antimeridian-west-half
cover.note: the western half of a straddling viewport, after the caller splits it. Longitude 180 lands in the LAST column (index 1023) because the encoder's cells are half-open and the top edge has nowhere above it to go.

cover.name: antimeridian-east-half
cover.note: and the eastern half, starting at column 0. The two halves share no cell, so the union is an exact cover of the seam.

supersession.note: Which of several events sharing (kind, pubkey, d) is the head. NIP-01 leaves the tie unspecified; this protocol does not.
supersession.rule: highest created_at wins; on a tie the LOWEST event id wins

createdAtMonotonicity.note: nextCreatedAt(lastPublished, nowSeconds) is the ONLY place a publisher may derive created_at for an addressable event. A skewed or rewound clock otherwise writes a head that can never be superseded, and the publisher still sees OK from the relay.
